target_customer: Robot builders in manufacturing, lab automation, education and humanoid projects who buy actuators
problem: Most robot joints estimate force from motor current, so robots cannot feel what they touch, and force sensing actuators are expensive.
business_model: Hardware sales of actuators, pre-orders open

founders.name: Enrico Milletti
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; education not listed.

competitors.name: Robotiq
competitors.what: Tactile fingertip sensors for grippers launched January 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating torque sensing into a low cost gearbox while shipping in volume is hardware engineering with manufacturing risk for a one person team.

defensibility.rationale: Design and manufacturing know-how could be hard to copy quickly, but patents and customer lock-in are not shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sensor makers sell add on force sensors; no source shows them bundling sensing into low cost actuators as of late 2026.

market_need_then: Physical AI and low cost training arms grew quickly in 2026; the company says over 60,000 units were requested in pre-orders within a month, a self reported and unverified figure.

branding.domain_note: Uses silicamachines.com (suffix); exact silica.com not used

brand_strength.rationale: Headline Today's robots are numb is a memorable framing, but no external press on the brand exists beyond one launch article.

outcome_analysis: Silica is a one person Fall 2026 hardware startup with no public exit. Pre-order interest is self reported and production is scheduled for January 2027, so delivery and manufacturing are the main open questions. Too early for an outcome verdict.
notes: Funding aggregators disagree and no company or press source confirms any round, so no round is recorded. Dealroom lists $125K seed (single aggregator); Fondo says the website names Founders Inc. and UP.Partners as backers without amounts. Samples ship February per launch and production January 2027 per site. Founder education not found. Undated competitor sources omitted from the list: Bota Systems.
